question: How much will Crude Oil Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 10-trading-day (front-month WTI % return minus S&P 500 % return) spreads, restricted to high-oil-vol regimes (OVX>45); that class centers near zero (slightly negative, ~-0.5, from front-month roll drag) with a very wide spread. Window has not started (0% elapsed at Now). Median shaded to -1.5 because CLV26 expires Sep 22 inside the window and the curve is in steep Hormuz backwardation, so a naive continuous front-month series takes a downward roll jump; plus post-spike risk-premium decay after WTI ran $78 (Aug 7) -> $104 (Sep 14), OPEC+ meeting Oct 4, and a Fed hike Sep 15-16. Offsetting upside for the spread: equities face a hiking Fed at 3.4% CPI, $100+ oil, Sep/Oct seasonality, and the S&P is already 1.8% off its Aug 13 high, so an equity drawdown alone can push the spread positive. Almost all variance is the oil leg: the Salalah Iran-GCC talks were postponed indefinitely Sep 13, so both a de-escalation deal (fast unwind of a ~$25 war premium) and loss of actual production remain live within the window. Market check: Kalshi prices daily/monthly WTI levels only (no spread contract, no matching threshold/deadline/source), Polymarket and Manifold have nothing - treated as evidence, not an anchor. Open bounds priced for a Hormuz reopening deal (below) and a production-loss escalation (above).

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the percent price return of Crude Oil Futures minus the percent price return of S&P 500 Futures over the stated window, not off spot crude, not off a cash equity index. Units are percentage points. Note the front-month contract question: WTI Oct-2026 (CLV26) last trade date is Sep 22, 2026 - INSIDE the window - so whether the series is a naive stitched front-month continuous (which gaps at the roll) or a roll-adjusted index matters; the WTI curve is reported in steep backwardation (a '$35 curve gap' front-to-deferred is cited in trade commentary), so the direction and size of any roll gap is material. EVENT WINDOW: Sep 21 -> Oct 2, 2026 per the criteria; as of 2026-09-14T17:54Z, 0% elapsed (window opens in ~7 days).

EVIDENCE:
- WTI traded 103.83 on 2026-09-14, +3.77% on the day; 30-day range Aug 14-Sep 14 was 79.62 to 104.46 (TradingEconomics, 2026-09-14).

Under discussion: a temporary arrangement with ships entering via Iranian waters and exiting via Omani waters; diplomats say a US-Iran agreement is ultimately needed for full reopening.
- S&P 500 closed 7,656.98 on Fri 2026-09-11, -0.8% on the week and -1.8% below its 2026-08-13 record close; it had fallen four straight sessions into Sep 10-11 before steadying (Seeking Alpha; InstaForex 2026-09-14).

- Volatility: OVX peaked ~126 in early April 2026 (WTI ran ~$70 to $111+ Feb 28-early April), roughly halved to ~60 by mid-year, ~67 on Jul 30, and 47.17 at the Aug 18 close; June 18-Jul 18 range was 39.73-63.76. BASE RATES / DISPERSION INPUTS:
- Class 'all two-week windows, any regime' (front-month WTI return minus S&P return, ~2015-2025): centers within about half a point of zero, mildly negative from front-month roll drag; the 10-90 span of that spread is on the order of 17 points, driven almost entirely by the oil leg (oil 10-day SD ~7%, equity ~3.2%, correlation mildly positive).
- Class 'two-week windows conditional on OVX above ~45' (the applicable conditioning variable here): the oil leg's 10-day SD scales to ~10-12% at OVX 50-60, and the oil-equity correlation flips mildly NEGATIVE in a supply-shock regime, both of which widen the spread relative to the unconditional class.
- Component anchor from the current regime itself: WTI moved +33% over the five weeks Aug 7 -> Sep 14, and single-day moves of 2-4% have been routine; the Feb 28 -> early April episode ran $70 -> $111 then retraced.
- Historical analogues for post-spike two-week paths in the same class: March 2022 (WTI ~$130 -> ~$95 within two weeks) and June 2025 (sharp give-back on a ceasefire) show the downside can be as violent as the upside; equally, the 2026 Feb-April leg shows sustained multi-week continuation is also in the class.

STATUS QUO OUTCOME: the strait stays blocked with no deal and no new production loss, oil holds roughly where it is, equities chop around the Fed decision, and the spread lands near its unconditional class center - i.e. a small number of either sign, not a large one.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: any prediction market on this spread or on relative oil-vs-equity returns (Kalshi lists only daily/monthly WTI LEVEL markets; Polymarket and Manifold title searches returned nothing); a current mid-September OVX print (most recent found is the Aug 18 close); the exact CLV26-CLX26 calendar spread in dollars; the precise roll convention of the series used to resolve this question; any scheduled OPEC+ or IEA event falling inside Sep 21 - Oct 2; a rescheduled date for the postponed Salalah meeting.
calls.reference_class: Two-week (10-trading-day) differences between front-month WTI crude futures percent price return and S&P 500 futures percent price return, conditioned on high crude-vol regimes (OVX above ~45)

calls.reasoning: Reference class first: 10-trading-day front-month crude minus S&P futures price-return spreads during war/supply-shock oil regimes (1990-91 Gulf, 2003 Iraq, 2008, 2011 Libya, 2022 Russia-Ukraine, 2025 Israel-Iran) have a median near zero and a very wide 10-90 band; so the anchor is 'no edge on direction, enormous dispersion'. The current regime is at or beyond the upper end of that class: Hormuz effectively closed since late Feb 2026 (~20% of global supply), Saudi East-West pipeline shut, Saudi output at post-1990 lows, WTI +20% on the month to ~$101-104. I shade the median slightly negative (-0.8pp) for three small, partly offsetting reasons: the S&P's ~+0.4%/2wk drift, mild mean-reversion after a parabolic geopolitical spike with a risk premium already embedded, and roll-gap risk (CLV26 expires Sep 22, curve steeply backwardated) if the resolution series is an unadjusted continuous front-month - offset by positive roll yield if it IS roll-adjusted. Left skew comes from a live discrete catalyst: Iran/Oman are reportedly close to a Hormuz reopening framework, which would strip a large premium in one session while simultaneously lifting equities, i.e. both legs move the spread the same way. Escalation (more tanker/pipeline strikes) is the mirror risk but adds less at the margin because the supply is already cut off. Market check: no contract prices this spread - Polymarket and Kalshi run WTI level markets only (monthly/daily/year-end, plus Polymarket's new oil perps), none with an equity leg or this window, so no anchor was used. Main caveat: the resolution criteria field is blank, so the exact instrument and roll convention are unknown, which widens rather than narrows my band.

SUBJECT: 10-trading-day return difference, Crude Oil Futures minus S&P 500 Futures, Sep 21 - Oct 2 2026, in percentage points.

EVENT WINDOW: Sep 21 2026 -> Oct 2 2026 (20:00Z) per the question criteria; as of Now 2026-09-14T17:54:35Z, 0% elapsed - the window opens in ~6.9 days. Ten NYMEX/CME trading sessions.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the two futures return series named in the question, not off spot WTI and not off the S&P 500 cash index. The question text supplies no ticker, no exchange, and no statement of whether the crude series is roll-adjusted. Mechanically relevant: NYMEX WTI October 2026 (CLV26) expires on or about Sep 22 2026, i.e. inside the window, so a naive front-month continuous quote would book the Oct->Nov price gap as a return while a back-adjusted or index-style series would book it as carry. E-mini S&P rolled ESU26->ESZ26 at the Sep 18 quad-witching, before the window opens, so the equity leg spans a single contract.

STATUS QUO OUTCOME: both legs are exchange-traded futures over ten sessions; absent new information each is approximately a martingale, so the difference absent news is near zero plus carry and drift terms of order 1pp.

EVIDENCE - SUPPLY SIDE

Five-to-six weeks from Sep 11 lands mid-to-late October, after the window closes.
- Since Feb 2026 US-Israel strikes on Iran, Strait of Hormuz flows are down from >20 mb/d to an estimated 6-9 mb/d (Al Jazeera, Sep 14 2026). The E-W pipeline was the principal workaround for that disruption.
- IEA warned Brent could reach $150/bbl if inventories draw to critical levels; a research firm flagged Yanbu itself going offline as the disaster case, with global refining capacity already tight (Al Jazeera, Sep 14 2026).
- Iraq dismissed a military commander and opened an investigation into the launch site (Al Jazeera, Sep 2026).

calls.reference_class: All 10-trading-day windows since 2000 of (front-month WTI crude futures total return minus S&P 500 futures total return), with the dispersion conditioned on the sub-class of windows in high-oil-volatility regimes (WTI 1M implied vol or OVX above 45)

calls.reasoning: Difference of two near-martingale futures legs over ten sessions, so the center sits near zero and all the content is dispersion. The conditioned reference class centers about -0.5pp (equity drift plus front-month roll drag) with a very wide band. I shade the median to -1.0: CLV26 expires ~Sep 22 inside the window into a steeply backwardated curve, so a naive continuous price series books a negative gap, weighted ~60% for convention uncertainty; the S&P's ~+0.4%/2wk drift subtracts too. Offsetting upward is the one catalyst concretely timed inside the window - Yanbu's 5-7 days of stored crude against a 5-6 week E-W pipeline repair, i.e. a Saudi export constraint could bite right as the window opens. The left tail stays fatter in the interior because premium unwinds outrun premium accumulation (Aug 7: -7% in a week on reopening anticipation alone; Jun 2025: -12% in one ceasefire session) and OPEC+ meets Oct 4-5 just past the close, but the Salalah ministerial was postponed indefinitely on Sep 13 and Iran conditions reopening on sanctions relief plus reparations, so a full deal inside ten sessions is unlikely. Negative oil-equity correlation in this regime amplifies both tails rather than damping them.
calls.reconciliation: Disputes were: (a) whether the resolution series is roll-adjusted - unsettleable this run, criteria field blank, carried as ~60/40 toward unadjusted and as extra width rather than resolved by fiat; (b) Run 3 double-counting backwardation as both +2%/mo carry and a -2pp roll artifact - these are mutually exclusive conventions, only one applies, so its move to a 0.0 median is partly unsupported and I land at -1.0; (c) conflicting front-month quotes - $103.83 / $101.56 / ~$102 are consistent for Sep 14, while the CME $91.30 October print is stale early-September research material; (d) OPEC+ Oct 4 vs Oct 5 - immaterial, both outside the window, only positioning ahead of it falls inside; (e) 'Iran-Oman close to a deal' vs 'Salalah postponed indefinitely' - both true and compatible, net read is that a reopening inside ten sessions is unlikely, so the left tail is priced but not enlarged; (f) tail asymmetry - pure judgment, resolved by noting the Yanbu 5-7 day storage clock expires as the window opens, which the runs underweighted, so I price the upper escape (0.06) above the lower (0.05) while keeping the interior left tail fatter. Dispersion recomputed from implied vols rather than carried forward, landing at 26pp, inside the runs' 24-26 range. No web access this run; no human market prices this spread on any venue the runs checked.
